accepted.name: txs_normalized
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  "hash" AS hash,
  "nonce" AS nonce,
  "transaction_index" AS transaction_index,
  "from_address" AS from_address,
  "to_address" AS to_address,
  "value" AS value,
  "gas" AS gas,
  "gas_price" AS gas_price,
  "input" AS input,
  "receipt_cumulative_gas_used" AS receipt_cumulative_gas_used,
  "receipt_gas_used" AS receipt_gas_used,
  "receipt_contract_address" AS receipt_contract_address,
  "receipt_root" AS receipt_root,
  "receipt_status" AS receipt_status,
  "block_timestamp" AS block_timestamp,
  "block_number" AS block_number,
  "block_hash" AS block_hash,
  -- derived: value in native stored numeric (already numeric type) kept as-is; keep a short flag for contract creation
  CASE WHEN "to_address" IS NULL OR "to_address" = '' THEN TRUE ELSE FALSE END AS is_contract_creation
FROM ETHEREUM_BLOCKCHAIN.ETHEREUM_BLOCKCHAIN.TRANSACTIONS
accepted.description: Normalized projection of TRANSACTIONS with consistent, typed column names and common derived measures (value_eth as numeric, gas_used, receipt_status). Use this to join transactions to other tables or to compute aggregates without repeatedly re-aliasing base columns. | Use for: transaction-level aggregations (counts, volumes, gas usage); join transactions to blocks / traces / logs; identify contract-creation transactions

accepted.name: blocks_basic
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT

  "hash" AS hash,
  "parent_hash" AS parent_hash,
  "timestamp" AS timestamp,
  "miner" AS miner,
  "difficulty" AS difficulty,
  "total_difficulty" AS total_difficulty,
  "size" AS size,
  "extra_data" AS extra_data,
  "gas_limit" AS gas_limit,
  "gas_used" AS gas_used,
  "transaction_count" AS transaction_count
FROM ETHEREUM_BLOCKCHAIN.ETHEREUM_BLOCKCHAIN.BLOCKS
accepted.description: Clean projection of BLOCKS exposing key block attributes and common measures. Useful to enrich event-level rows with block-level context or to compute block-level aggregates. | Use for: block-level summaries (gas usage, transaction counts); joining blocks to transactions/traces/logs by block_number or block_hash; time-series analysis of block metrics

accepted.name: token_transfers_normalized
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  "token_address" AS token_address,
  "from_address" AS from_address,
  "to_address" AS to_address,
  "value" AS raw_value,
  "transaction_hash" AS transaction_hash,
  "log_index" AS log_index,
  "block_timestamp" AS block_timestamp,
  "block_number" AS block_number,
  "block_hash" AS block_hash
FROM ETHEREUM_BLOCKCHAIN.ETHEREUM_BLOCKCHAIN.TOKEN_TRANSFERS
grain: transaction_hash + log_index (one row per token transfer event)
accepted.description: Normalized token transfer events with safely aliased columns. Value left as stored (VARCHAR) because token decimals vary; join to TOKENS to normalize amounts. Use for token flow and token-holder analyses. | Use for: token transfer volume per token or address; join token transfers to token metadata for decimals/symbol; identify token counterparties

accepted.name: tokens_latest_by_address
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  "address" AS address,
  "symbol" AS symbol,
  "name" AS name,
  "decimals" AS decimals,
  "total_supply" AS total_supply,
  "block_timestamp" AS block_timestamp,
  "block_number" AS block_number,
  "block_hash" AS block_hash,
  ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY "address" ORDER BY "block_number" DESC, "block_timestamp" DESC) AS address_row_number
FROM ETHEREUM_BLOCKCHAIN.ETHEREUM_BLOCKCHAIN.TOKENS
grain: address + address_row_number (one row per token snapshot; filter where address_row_number = 1 yields one row per token)
accepted.description: Latest token metadata snapshot per token address (ranked by block_number then block_timestamp). Useful when you need the most recent decimals/symbol/name per token for normalization and labeling. | Use for: obtain canonical token decimals/symbol for normalizing token_transfer.raw_value; token catalog and labeling

accepted.name: logs_flat_topics
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  "log_index" AS log_index,
  "transaction_hash" AS transaction_hash,
  "transaction_index" AS transaction_index,
  "address" AS address,
  "data" AS data,
  "topics" AS topics_variant,
  "block_timestamp" AS block_timestamp,
  "block_number" AS block_number,
  "block_hash" AS block_hash,
  -- extract up to four positional topics (NULL if absent), cast each variant element to VARCHAR using ::VARCHAR
  topics_array[0]::VARCHAR AS topic_0,
  topics_array[1]::VARCHAR AS topic_1,
  topics_array[2]::VARCHAR AS topic_2,
  topics_array[3]::VARCHAR AS topic_3
FROM ETHEREUM_BLOCKCHAIN.ETHEREUM_BLOCKCHAIN.LOGS,
LATERAL (
  SELECT ARRAY_AGG(f.value) AS topics_array
  FROM TABLE(FLATTEN(input => "topics")) f
) f
grain: transaction_hash + log_index (one row per log entry)
accepted.description: Logs with topics flattened (first 4 topics as separate columns) to simplify common log-topic queries. Uses VARIANT topics from LOGS; safe if topics are an array. Useful for event signature matching and filtering. | Use for: match logs by event signature (topic_0); filter logs for specific indexed parameters in topic_1..topic_3

accepted.name: contract_signatures_flat
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  "address" AS address,
  f.value::VARCHAR AS function_sighash,
  "is_erc20" AS is_erc20,
  "is_erc721" AS is_erc721,
  "block_timestamp" AS block_timestamp,
  "block_number" AS block_number,
  "block_hash" AS block_hash
FROM ETHEREUM_BLOCKCHAIN.ETHEREUM_BLOCKCHAIN.CONTRACTS c,
LATERAL FLATTEN(input => c."function_sighashes") f
grain: address + function_sighash (one row per discovered sighash per contract snapshot)
accepted.description: Explodes CONTRACTS.function_sighashes VARIANT into one row per (contract_address, sighash) so function signature presence can be queried. Useful for detecting contracts exposing specific function signatures. | Use for: search contracts exposing a particular function signature; compute counts of contracts exposing ERC-20/721-related signatures

accepted.name: token_transfers_with_token_metadata
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  tt.token_address AS token_address,
  tt.from_address AS from_address,
  tt.to_address AS to_address,
  tt.raw_value AS raw_value,
  tt.transaction_hash AS transaction_hash,
  tt.log_index AS log_index,
  tt.block_timestamp AS block_timestamp,
  tt.block_number AS block_number,
  tt.block_hash AS block_hash,
  tok.symbol AS symbol,
  tok.name AS name,
  tok.decimals AS decimals,
  tok.total_supply AS total_supply
FROM (
  SELECT
    "token_address" AS token_address,
    "from_address" AS from_address,
    "to_address" AS to_address,
    "value" AS raw_value,
    "transaction_hash" AS transaction_hash,
    "log_index" AS log_index,
    "block_timestamp" AS block_timestamp,
    "block_number" AS block_number,
    "block_hash" AS block_hash
  FROM ETHEREUM_BLOCKCHAIN.ETHEREUM_BLOCKCHAIN.TOKEN_TRANSFERS
) tt
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT
    address AS address,
    symbol AS symbol,
    name AS name,
    decimals AS decimals,
    total_supply AS total_supply,
    block_timestamp AS block_timestamp,
    block_number AS block_number,
    block_hash AS block_hash
  FROM (
    SELECT
      "address" AS address,
      "symbol" AS symbol,
      "name" AS name,
      "decimals" AS decimals,
      "total_supply" AS total_supply,
      "block_timestamp" AS block_timestamp,
      "block_number" AS block_number,
      "block_hash" AS block_hash,
      ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY "address" ORDER BY "block_number" DESC, "block_timestamp" DESC) AS rn
    FROM ETHEREUM_BLOCKCHAIN.ETHEREUM_BLOCKCHAIN.TOKENS
  ) t
  WHERE rn = 1
) tok
  ON LOWER(tt.token_address) = LOWER(tok.address)
grain: transaction_hash + log_index (one row per token transfer)
accepted.description: Token transfers joined to the latest token metadata per token address (joinable on token_address). Exposes decimals and symbol to enable downstream normalization of raw_value. Keeps transfer grain. | Use for: normalize token transfer amounts to human-readable decimals; token volume and holder analyses using token metadata

accepted.name: top_transactions_by_value_rank
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  "hash" AS hash,
  "block_number" AS block_number,
  "block_timestamp" AS block_timestamp,
  "from_address" AS from_address,
  "to_address" AS to_address,
  "value" AS value,
  ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY "block_number" ORDER BY "value" DESC NULLS LAST, "transaction_index" ASC) AS block_tx_value_rank
FROM ETHEREUM_BLOCKCHAIN.ETHEREUM_BLOCKCHAIN.TRANSACTIONS
grain: hash + block_tx_value_rank (one row per transaction; rank indicates position within its block)
accepted.description: Per-block rank of transactions ordered by value descending. Exposes a block_tx_value_rank that can be filtered (e.g., rank <= K) downstream to get top-K transactions per block. | Use for: select top-K highest-value transactions per block; distribution of transaction values within blocks
